title: Raghubir v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Sanjay Misra, J.; Anant Kumar, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; petitioner relegated to Clause 6.5.
headnote: A writ challenging an electricity bill on disputed questions of fact is not the proper forum. The consumer may avail the remedy under Clause 6.5 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
facts: Raghubir challenged a 25 March 2014 electricity bill issued by the Executive Engineer of Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd., Agra, by a writ petition in the Allahabad High Court. The licensee raised a preliminary objection that the billing dispute could be more effectively decided under Clause 6.5 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Counsel for both sides were heard. The Court treated the challenge as raising disputed questions of fact against the impugned bill.

holding_units.holding: Where a writ petition disputes an electricity bill and raises disputed questions of fact, those questions are better decided by the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ is disposed of with liberty to the petitioner to avail that remedy.

not_decided.point: Correctness of the 25 March 2014 electricity bill
not_decided.note: Merits left to the Clause 6.5 authority; the writ was not decided on the bill.
